questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve, do these actions separately. Never brake while swerving. This can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle to control it well?

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Keep your arms straight when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should bend slightly when you grip the handlebars. Press your knees against the gas tank to help you stay balanced.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast a small vehicle is going or how far away it is. Do not assume that drivers of large vehicles can accurately see your speed and location.

questions.question: There is an oily strip in the center of a lane. What does this mean?

options.text: You should avoid it at all times.
It usually has good traction, unless it is raining.
You should only ride on it if another vehicle is in the lane with you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually has good traction, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip in the center of the road usually has enough traction for safe riding, unless it is raining. The strip is usually about two feet wide. You can ride on either side of it and still be in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: You are in a crash that damages more than $1,000 in property. What must you do?

options.text: File a report only if you plan to tell your insurance company.
Send a crash report to the DMV.
Call the highway department.

questions.correctAnswerText: Send a crash report to the DMV.
questions.explanation: If you are in a crash with more than $1,000 in property damage, you must send a report to the DMV. The DMV can take action if the crash involves an uninsured vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must stop completely.
You may go through slowly and carefully.
You must let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop completely.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop completely and wait for a green signal before turning in that direction.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.
Follow other vehicles more closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes at night, slow down and leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead. Use their headlights to see farther down the road. Be ready to change your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycles pulling trailers?

options.text: They cannot use carpool lanes.
They can travel in any highway lane.
They cannot go faster than 25 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot use carpool lanes.
questions.explanation: In California, motorcycles towing trailers cannot use carpool lanes. They should stay in the right lane, except when passing. Do not go faster than 55 mph when towing a trailer.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: During the day.
At dusk.
At night.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective gear when riding, even in daylight.

questions.question: A dog is chasing your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Ride slowly toward the dog, then speed up quickly as it gets close.
Turn sharply to avoid the dog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slowly toward the dog, then speed up quickly as it gets close.
questions.explanation: If a dog approaches your motorcycle, slow down and shift to a lower gear as you get near it. Quickly speed up as the dog comes close to you.

questions.question: Is eye protection required?

options.text: Yes, it is required for all riders.
No, but it is recommended.
Only for new riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all motorcycle riders to wear eye protection. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road will split into two separate directions ahead.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the road is slippery.
When the sun is shining.
When you can stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is slippery.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance on slippery roads because your motorcycle needs more space to stop. Also increase distance if you cannot see ahead or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Stop completely and go only when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go only when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you tell a passenger before riding?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you do.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.
questions.explanation: Have the passenger mount after you start the engine. The passenger should sit as close to you as possible without crowding you and hold firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should you wear while riding?

options.text: Hearing protection to stop damage from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.
A baseball cap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to stop damage from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: How should you look through a turn?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders.
Turn just your head.
Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Look through turns by turning only your head. Keep your eyes level with the horizon and do not move your shoulders.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when being passed?

options.text: The right side of the lane
The center of the lane
The left side of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center of the lane
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving closer to the passing vehicle creates a dangerous situation for both of you.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of wheels a motorcycle can have?

options.text: Two wheels
Three wheels
Four wheels

questions.correctAnswerText: Three wheels
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a motor vehicle with a seat for the rider and no more than three wheels.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: On the outside of the curve
On the inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose your lane position based on traffic and road conditions, and adjust as needed.

questions.question: What is a main cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
Leaving the road while trying to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-vehicle crashes is turning too wide in a curve or turn. Turning too wide can make a motorcycle leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: What riding formation should you use in a group?

options.text: Always single-file.
It depends on the situation.
Always staggered.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: Use staggered formation most of the time. Switch to single-file when taking a curve, making a turn, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What should you do when riding over grooved pavement in a work zone?

options.text: Look down to watch for road surface changes.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up in a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle gives the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is ahead.

questions.question: What is the minimum license needed to operate a moped?

options.text: Class M1
Class M2
Class C

questions.correctAnswerText: Class M2
questions.explanation: A Class M2 license lets you operate a motorized bicycle, moped, or motorized scooter. A Class M1 license lets you operate these plus any two-wheel motorcycle. A Class C license lets you operate a motorcycle with a side car, three-wheel motorcycle, or motorized scooter.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, who goes first?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to proceed.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked intersection with no traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Which statement about motorized scooters is true?

options.text: Can only be operated during the day.
Can be operated without a driver license.
Can be operated with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be operated with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: An engine will seize because of:

options.text: Not enough oil.
Not enough fuel.
Improper tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not enough oil.
questions.explanation: Engines seize when there is not enough oil. Without oil, the engine's moving parts cannot slide smoothly and the engine overheats.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red traffic light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to all crossing traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when safe.
